scope: GitHub Actions artifact retention as one candidate second durability domain for recovering role-local semantic witness after Git-object / repository-history loss
question: Can GitHub Actions artifacts provide an independent, zero-cost, zero-finite-quota durability witness that survives the tested same-domain Git-object loss and closes whole-repository-loss liveness?
observations: GitHub documents Actions artifact retention as configurable and finite rather than indefinite.
A finite-retention artifact cannot satisfy this Phase-1 run's zero-finite-quota durability gate for an unbounded recovery witness.

result.independent_from_git_object_reachability: plausibly separate storage layer, but not established as independent from full repository deletion/recreation in this slice

o_comparison.reason: This slice tests the candidate durability class and does not mutate or broaden O comparison beyond prior verified scope.

uncertainty: This does not prove that every external durability mechanism fails.
This slice does not establish whether retained Actions artifacts survive all forms of repository deletion/recreation.
continuation: Next run: test one externally anchored, publicly readable, role-authorized durability witness class outside the repository/GitHub Actions retention domain that can plausibly satisfy zero cost and zero finite quota; if no such authorized surface exists under current policy, record the exact authority-policy blocker without relaxing Phase-1 gates.
